newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IRI to transfer Stet to Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IRI to transfer Stet to Treasury.

text.p: Italian industrial holding IRI will transfer its stake in telecommunications group Stet to the Treasury for a minimum of 14.53 trillion lire ($9.3 billion), the Treasury said on Monday.
It said in a statement that it would pay IRI three trillion lire by the end of December and would hand over the balance by the end of June 1997.
It said the cash was to be used exclusively to reduce IRI's huge debts.

Stet shares were suspended at 6,330 lire on the Milan bourse pending the announcement. Shares in Telecom Italia, Stet's operating unit, were also suspended at 3,570 and both were due to resume trading at 1340 GMT, market regulator Consob said.
The Treasury said the transfer of shares in Stet, Europe's fourth-biggest telephone concern, would take place by the end of December. IRI holds 61.27 percent of Stet ordinary shares.

Italy had planned to privatise Stet by the end of March next year but acknowledged last month that its goal was no longer feasible. It now plans to merge Stet with Telecom Italia and sell off the combined entity late in 1997.

The transfer of Stet shares to the Treasury is an interim measure designed to ease pressure on IRI, which faces a loss of up to three trillion lire in 1996. Under a 1993 accord with the European Union, IRI must cut its debt to below five trillion lire by the year-end from its end-1995 level of 22.5 trillion. ($1=1,555 lire)
